name: Switchgrass Crossing
headline: Volunteers of America National Services is developing Switchgrass Crossing, a new 45-unit, four-story apartment building for adults 55+ earning 30% to 60% AMI, on a former parking lot at 3800 S. Mason St. by the MAX Horsetooth Station in Fort Collins. It won 2025 Round One federal 9%, state and TOC credits from CHFA.
why_it_matters: It is a transit-site senior deal that stacked several small public pieces on top of the 9% credit: about $1.2M from the city's competitive process, a $792K state TOC infrastructure grant and a city fee credit. VOANS announced its financing closing in May 2026 and a $26M project.

status.label: Financing closed (announced May 2026); construction start not confirmed
status.detail: VOANS announced on 2026-05-27 that it had closed the financing, with construction expected to begin in June 2026 and completion in summer 2027. No public building permit, groundbreaking record or construction photo was found to confirm that work has started.

next_step: Look for a City of Fort Collins building permit for 3800 S. Mason St., or a VOANS or city groundbreaking notice, to confirm that construction started in mid-2026.

key_numbers.meaning: 39 one-bedroom and 6 two-bedroom units at 30% to 60% AMI (average 52% AMI, per the applicant).
About $16M over the 10-year credit period, plus $650,000 state credit and $58,500 TOC credit.
VOANS's figure when it announced the financing closing in May 2026.

key_numbers.value: About $2M in local and state gap money
key_numbers.meaning: $1,215,574 from Fort Collins's 2025 competitive funding process and a $792K state Transit Oriented Communities infrastructure grant for site utilities and stormwater.

facts.value: 3800 S. Mason St., Fort Collins, CO 80525
N, OA: new construction, older adult
A 1.4-acre former parking lot along the South College Avenue corridor, a few miles south of downtown
The applicant says the site is zoned for the project as a use by right, with no public hearing process
One four-story wood-frame building on a slab, with two elevators, surface parking, a courtyard, raised garden beds and a dog run
About a 3-minute walk to the MAX bus rapid transit Horsetooth Station; Transfort service is free to riders

All-electric with rooftop solar; designed for Enterprise Green Communities, DOE Efficient New Homes (Zero Energy Ready) and ENERGY STAR Multifamily New Construction. VOANS says it is its first all-electric building in Colorado
The applicant says the site is in neither a QCT nor a DDA, so the deal works only as a 9%
The applicant elected the Average Income test

money.source: Colorado standard state housing tax credit
City of Fort Collins competitive process (affordable housing)
money.note: 97% of a $1,250,000 request, ranked #5 of the housing proposals. It is on the 2025-06-17 Council consent calendar as Resolution 2025-065, which funds the spring cycle from CDBG, HOME and the city's Affordable Housing Fund. The packet does not show which program pays for this project.

money.source: Colorado Transit Oriented Communities Infrastructure (TOCI) grant
money.note: Awarded to the City of Fort Collins in partnership with VOA for on-site utility connections, stormwater upgrades and a detention pond.

money.source: City tap and impact fee credit
money.note: Per the applicant, for the five 30% AMI units. Tap and impact fees run almost $30,000 per unit.
The applicant calls it a sizeable sponsor commitment.
VOANS thanks First Bank; that it is the lender is inferred.
VOANS thanks Enterprise Partners; that it is the syndicator is inferred. The applicant also plans solar and 45L energy credits.

parties.role: Sponsor (as CHFA prints it) and developer
parties.name: Volunteers of America National Services (VOANS)
Housing Catalyst (the Fort Collins housing authority). VOANS calls this its second Fort Collins deal with Housing Catalyst; the terms of the partnership are not public
Housing Catalyst, City of Fort Collins, State of Colorado, Enterprise Partners, First Bank

background.text: VOANS pitches the project as a follow-on to Cadence, its 2020 LIHTC senior building in Fort Collins, which has a waitlist of more than 300 people. Its other local senior property is Sanctuary, about 1.6 miles away.

The market study's overall capture rate is 26.3%, above CHFA's 25% guideline. The applicant argues that the true rate is lower because CHFA counts only renters 62+ while the building takes 55+. The study projects lease-up at 11.25 units a month and stabilization within four months.
The Phase I found no recognized environmental condition. Because the site was a parking lot, VOA committed to watch for soil staining or odors during work.
The applicant requested a cost basis waiver (Attachment 6 of the application, which is not public).
At application the team expected a building permit in February 2026 and closing in March 2026. VOANS announced the closing on 2026-05-27.

The design team took part in the City of Fort Collins Integrated Design Assistance Program. Amenities include a fourth-floor resident lounge, community room, business center, covered porch, terrace and indoor bike storage at one space per resident.
On-site staff will offer benefit and transportation navigation, technology classes and financial literacy. Residents can also use VOA's Fort Collins meals, veteran and older-adult programs.
Fort Collins's Human Services and Housing Funding Board describes the project as 45 new units for low-income seniors below 60% AMI.

discrepancies.text: The application narrative gives the site a walk score of 98, while the TOC narrative cites a walkability score of 76 from the market study.
The application narrative says Cadence opened in 2022, while the VOANS closing release says it opened in 2021.
VOANS puts the top of the income range at about $62K (60% AMI), while the state TOCI announcement says about $54K for a one-person household.

open_questions: Whether construction actually started in June 2026: no building permit, groundbreaking notice or site photo was found.
Housing Catalyst's role (ownership, a property tax exemption or financing) is not described in any public record found.
Which programs fund the $1,215,574 city award, and the loan terms and covenant length.
Amounts of the VOA Capital Magnet Fund loan, the First Bank debt and the tax credit equity, plus the equity price.
Whether the Shopworks/BC Builders team from the application stayed in place at closing.
Length of the CHFA affordability period (LURA) and whether any vouchers apply. The narrative mentions none.
